walkthroughs.body_html: Shallow depth of field (wide aperture like f/2.8) isolates a subject from a blurred background — useful for portraits. Deep depth of field (narrow aperture like f/16) keeps near and far sharp — useful for landscapes.

Different light sources have different colour temperatures. Tungsten bulbs look orange, daylight neutral, shade slightly blue. White balance tells the camera what should look white so other colours render correctly.

JPEG is compressed and ready to share but throws away data. RAW files keep all the sensor information so you can recover detail in highlights and shadows during editing — but they need processing and take more space.
